action.short_description: Changing sanctuary approval rules for cables and special-use permits
action.compact_description: The bill would limit separate sanctuary approvals for cable activities already authorized by an effective federal or state approval, preserve interagency cooperation, and remove two general special-use permit terms. Membership remains unaccepted.
action.meaning:
The February11,2026 question was passage of H.R.261 in its House-passed form. The whole bill combines a conditional undersea fiber-optic cable permitting restriction with changes to general sanctuary special-use permit terms. It is not only a vote on a selected cable benefit, and House passage is not enactment or a completed project.
New section310A, notwithstanding other provisions of the National Marine Sanctuaries Act, would prevent the Secretary of Commerce from prohibiting or requiring a permit, including a special-use permit, or other authorization for the enumerated cable activities in a national marine sanctuary IF another Federal OR State agency has issued a license, lease or permit that is in effect authorizing those activities. The listed installation, continued presence, operation, maintenance, repair and recovery activities retain their scope. An expired, unrelated or merely requested approval does not satisfy the stated predicate. This is not a blanket exemption for every cable without other agency authorization, nor does the bill itself issue a license, choose a route, establish ownership or guarantee a project.
The bill expressly preserves interagency cooperation under304(d) for the described federal agency actions involving these cable activities. The retained subsection covers actions inside or outside a sanctuary, including licensed private activities, likely to destroy, cause loss of or injure a sanctuary resource. It retains early agency statements ordinarily at least45daysbeforefinalapproval unless a different schedule is agreed, and reasonable/prudent alternative recommendations within45daysofcompleteinformation where the Secretary finds likely harm. These are distinct clocks, not a single automatic45dayapproval. The agency head must consult and explain a decision not to follow recommended alternatives; if another action causes the specified harm, the source retains prevention/mitigation and restoration/replacement duties in the stated manner. Consultation is not abolished merely because a separate sanctuary permit cannot be required for an otherwise covered cable activity.
Section3 deletes1441(c)(2) and(c)(3) from the general special-use permit terms: the five-year maximum unless renewed, and the term requiring activities not destroy, cause loss of or injure sanctuary resources. Those deletions apply to special-use permits generally, not only cable permits. Remaining(c)(1)compatibility with sanctuary-designation purposes and protection of sanctuary resources is retained, and the existing insurance/equivalent-bond and hold-harmless term is redesignated, not deleted. The selected baseline's separate issuance/public-notice and fee clauses are not struck by this amendment. No finding is made that every other legal protection, damage liability, authorization or possible charge disappears, or that a permit automatically lasts forever.
This is a change in sanctuary approval constraints and permit terms, not a finding that cables cause no harm, that any particular route is authorized, or that broadband capacity, cost, resilience, construction or environmental outcomes have occurred. The candidate does not certify all current sanctuary regulations, another agency's individual licensing authority or project-specific compliance. A Yea supports passing this whole conditional cable/general-permit-term package; a Nay opposes it without identifying a preferred alternative or opposition to communications generally.
Infrastructure/Technology membership is an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal under the existing direct communications-infrastructure criterion. The whole action includes general sanctuary permit changes beyond cables; an independent taxonomy review must consider that broader environmental/permit scope. Source, whole-action and taxonomy review are required before acceptance or publication; no accepted methodology change follows.
limitations: Whole conditional cable rule plus general permit-term deletions; House passage is not enactment or project approval.
Other Federal OR State license/lease/permit must be issued, effective and authorize the listed activities; no blanket unlicensed-cable exemption.
Interagency cooperation, distinct45dayclocks and stated response/mitigation duties remain; no automatic approval.
General five-year and no-injury terms deleted across special-use permits, while compatibility and insurance/bond/hold-harmless terms remain.
No complete current legal/project-specific authority, universal immunity, fee waiver or actual communications/environmental outcome is certified.
Direct communications-infrastructure mapping remains unaccepted and must account for the broader general-permit scope.

R. 261 _______________________________________________________________________ AN ACT To amend the National Marine Sanctuaries Act to prohibit the Secretary of Commerce from prohibiting, or requiring any permit or other authorization for, the installation, continued presence, operation, maintenance, repair, or recovery of undersea fiber optic cables in a national marine sanctuary if such activities have been authorized by a Federal or State agency. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled, SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE. This Act may be cited as the ``Undersea Cable Protection Act of 2025''. SEC. 2. PROHIBITION ON PROHIBITING, OR REQUIRING PERMITS OR OTHER AUTHORIZATIONS FOR, UNDERSEA FIBER OPTIC CABLES AUTHORIZED BY A FEDERAL OR STATE AGENCY. The National Marine Sanctuaries Act (16 U.S.C. 1431 et seq.) is amended by inserting after section 310 the following: ``SEC. 310A. PROHIBITION ON PROHIBITING, OR REQUIRING PERMITS OR OTHER AUTHORIZATIONS FOR, UNDERSEA FIBER OPTIC CABLES AUTHORIZED BY A FEDERAL OR STATE AGENCY. ``(a) In General.--Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, the Secretary may not prohibit, or require any permit, including any special use permit, or other authorization for, the installation, continued presence, operation, maintenance, repair, or recovery of undersea fiber optic cables in a national marine sanctuary if a license, lease, or permit has been issued by a Federal or State agency, and is in effect, authorizing such installation, continued presence, operation, maintenance, repair, or recovery. ``(b) Interagency Cooperation.--Nothing in this section shall be construed as altering existing requirements regarding interagency cooperation under section 304(d) in any Federal agency action described in that section and involving the installation, continued presence, operation, maintenance, repair, or recovery of undersea fiber optic cables in a national marine sanctuary.''. SEC. 3. REMOVING RESTRICTIONS ON ACTIVITIES COVERED BY SANCTUARY SPECIAL USE PERMITS. Section 310(c) of National Marine Sanctuaries Act (16 U.S.C. 1441(c)) is amended-- (1) in paragraph (1), by adding ``and'' at the end; (2) by striking paragraphs (2) and (3); and (3) by redesignating paragraph (4) as paragraph (2). Passed the House of Representatives February 11, 2026. Attest: Clerk. 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. claim_source_map.locator: Exact identified governed version/operative extent; qualifications retained
claim_source_map.passage: §1441. Special use permits (a) Issuance of permits The Secretary may issue special use permits which authorize the conduct of specific activities in a national marine sanctuary if the Secretary determines such authorization is necessary— (1) to establish conditions of access to and use of any sanctuary resource; or (2) to promote public use and understanding of a sanctuary resource. (b) Public notice required The Secretary shall provide appropriate public notice before identifying any category of activity subject to a special use permit under subsection (a). (c) Permit terms A permit issued under this section— (1) shall authorize the conduct of an activity only if that activity is compatible with the purposes for which the sanctuary is designated and with protection of sanctuary resources; (2) shall not authorize the conduct of any activity for a period of more than 5 years unless renewed by the Secretary; (3) shall require that activities carried out under the permit be conducted in a manner that does not destroy, cause the loss of, or injure sanctuary resources; and (4) shall require the permittee to purchase and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance, or post an equivalent bond, against claims arising out of activities conducted under the permit and to agree to hold the United States harmless against such claims. (d) Fees (1) Assessment and collection The Secretary may assess and collect fees for the conduct of any activity under a permit issued under this section. (2) Amount The amount of a fee under this subsection shall be equal to the sum of— (A) costs incurred, or expected to be incurred, by the Secretary in issuing the permit; (B) costs incurred, or expected to be incurred, by the Secretary as a direct result of the conduct of the activity for which the permit is issued, including costs of monitoring the conduct of the activity; and (C) an amount which represents the fair market value of the use of the sanctuary resource. (3) Use of fees Amounts collected by the Secretary in the form of fees under this section may be used by the Secretary— (A) for issuing and administering permits under this section; and (B) for expenses of managing national marine sanctuaries. (4) Waiver or reduction of fees The Secretary may accept in-kind contributions in lieu of a fee under paragraph (2)(C), or waive or reduce any fee assessed under this subsection for any activity that does not derive profit from the access to or use of sanctuary resources.

claim_source_map.locator: Exact identified governed version/operative extent; qualifications retained
claim_source_map.passage: (d) Interagency cooperation (1) Review of agency actions (A) In general Federal agency actions internal or external to a national marine sanctuary, including private activities authorized by licenses, leases, or permits, that are likely to destroy, cause the loss of, or injure any sanctuary resource are subject to consultation with the Secretary. (B) Agency statements required Subject to any regulations the Secretary may establish each Federal agency proposing an action described in subparagraph (A) shall provide the Secretary with a written statement describing the action and its potential effects on sanctuary resources at the earliest practicable time, but in no case later than 45 days before the final approval of the action unless such Federal agency and the Secretary agree to a different schedule. (2) Secretary's recommended alternatives If the Secretary finds that a Federal agency action is likely to destroy, cause the loss of, or injure a sanctuary resource, the Secretary shall (within 45 days of receipt of complete information on the proposed agency action) recommend reasonable and prudent alternatives, which may include conduct of the action elsewhere, which can be taken by the Federal agency in implementing the agency action that will protect sanctuary resources. (3) Response to recommendations The agency head who receives the Secretary's recommended alternatives under paragraph (2) shall promptly consult with the Secretary on the alternatives. If the agency head decides not to follow the alternatives, the agency head shall provide the Secretary with a written statement explaining the reasons for that decision. (4) Failure to follow alternative If the head of a Federal agency takes an action other than an alternative recommended by the Secretary and such action results in the destruction of, loss of, or injury to a sanctuary resource, the head of the agency shall promptly prevent and mitigate further damage and restore or replace the sanctuary resource in a manner approved by the Secretary.

record.rationale: Complete261EH and retained1441permit/1434(d)cooperation units support an unaccepted communications-infrastructure candidate for the WHOLE cable/general-permit package. Preserve issued-and-effective other-agency approval, FederalORState, listed activities, surviving consultation and distinct45dayclocks, general rather than cable-only term deletions, and retained compatibility/insurance/bond terms. No universal permit exemption, immunity, lifetime term, current project approval or actual network/environmental outcome. The broader sanctuary-permit scope requires independent taxonomy review.

PROHIBITION ON PROHIBITING, OR REQUIRING PERMITS OR OTHER AUTHORIZATIONS FOR, UNDERSEA FIBER OPTIC CABLES AUTHORIZED BY A FEDERAL OR STATE AGENCY. ``(a) In General.--Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, the Secretary may not prohibit, or require any permit, including any special use permit, or other authorization for, the installation, continued presence, operation, maintenance, repair, or recovery of undersea fiber optic cables in a national marine sanctuary if a license, lease, or permit has been issued by a Federal or State agency, and is in effect, authorizing such installation, continued presence, operation, maintenance, repair, or recovery. ``(b) Interagency Cooperation.--Nothing in this section shall be construed as altering existing requirements regarding interagency cooperation under section 304(d) in any Federal agency action described in that section and involving the installation, continued presence, operation, maintenance, repair, or recovery of undersea fiber optic cables in a national marine sanctuary.''. SEC. 3. REMOVING RESTRICTIONS ON ACTIVITIES COVERED BY SANCTUARY SPECIAL USE PERMITS. Section 310(c) of National Marine Sanctuaries Act (16 U.S.C. 1441(c)) is amended-- (1) in paragraph (1), by adding ``and'' at the end; (2) by striking paragraphs (2) and (3); and (3) by redesignating paragraph (4) as paragraph (2). Passed the House of Representatives February 11, 2026. Attest: Clerk. 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. R. 261 _______________________________________________________________________ AN ACT To amend the National Marine Sanctuaries Act to prohibit the Secretary of Commerce from prohibiting, or requiring any permit or other authorization for, the installation, continued presence, operation, maintenance, repair, or recovery of undersea fiber optic cables in a national marine sanctuary if such activities have been authorized by a Federal or State agency.

Special use permits (a) Issuance of permits The Secretary may issue special use permits which authorize the conduct of specific activities in a national marine sanctuary if the Secretary determines such authorization is necessary— (1) to establish conditions of access to and use of any sanctuary resource; or (2) to promote public use and understanding of a sanctuary resource. (b) Public notice required The Secretary shall provide appropriate public notice before identifying any category of activity subject to a special use permit under subsection (a). (c) Permit terms A permit issued under this section— (1) shall authorize the conduct of an activity only if that activity is compatible with the purposes for which the sanctuary is designated and with protection of sanctuary resources; (2) shall not authorize the conduct of any activity for a period of more than 5 years unless renewed by the Secretary; (3) shall require that activities carried out under the permit be conducted in a manner that does not destroy, cause the loss of, or injure sanctuary resources; and (4) shall require the permittee to purchase and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance, or post an equivalent bond, against claims arising out of activities conducted under the permit and to agree to hold the United States harmless against such claims. (d) Fees (1) Assessment and collection The Secretary may assess and collect fees for the conduct of any activity under a permit issued under this section. (2) Amount The amount of a fee under this subsection shall be equal to the sum of— (A) costs incurred, or expected to be incurred, by the Secretary in issuing the permit; (B) costs incurred, or expected to be incurred, by the Secretary as a direct result of the conduct of the activity for which the permit is issued, including costs of monitoring the conduct of the activity; and (C) an amount which represents the fair market value of the use of the sanctuary resource. (3) Use of fees Amounts collected by the Secretary in the form of fees under this section may be used by the Secretary— (A) for issuing and administering permits under this section; and (B) for expenses of managing national marine sanctuaries. (4) Waiver or reduction of fees The Secretary may accept in-kind contributions in lieu of a fee under paragraph (2)(C), or waive or reduce any fee assessed under this subsection for any activity that does not derive profit from the access to or use of sanctuary resources.

claim_source_map.passage: (d) Interagency cooperation (1) Review of agency actions (A) In general Federal agency actions internal or external to a national marine sanctuary, including private activities authorized by licenses, leases, or permits, that are likely to destroy, cause the loss of, or injure any sanctuary resource are subject to consultation with the Secretary. (B) Agency statements required Subject to any regulations the Secretary may establish each Federal agency proposing an action described in subparagraph (A) shall provide the Secretary with a written statement describing the action and its potential effects on sanctuary resources at the earliest practicable time, but in no case later than 45 days before the final approval of the action unless such Federal agency and the Secretary agree to a different schedule. (2) Secretary's recommended alternatives If the Secretary finds that a Federal agency action is likely to destroy, cause the loss of, or injure a sanctuary resource, the Secretary shall (within 45 days of receipt of complete information on the proposed agency action) recommend reasonable and prudent alternatives, which may include conduct of the action elsewhere, which can be taken by the Federal agency in implementing the agency action that will protect sanctuary resources. (3) Response to recommendations The agency head who receives the Secretary's recommended alternatives under paragraph (2) shall promptly consult with the Secretary on the alternatives. If the agency head decides not to follow the alternatives, the agency head shall provide the Secretary with a written statement explaining the reasons for that decision. (4) Failure to follow alternative If the head of a Federal agency takes an action other than an alternative recommended by the Secretary and such action results in the destruction of, loss of, or injury to a sanctuary resource, the head of the agency shall promptly prevent and mitigate further damage and restore or replace the sanctuary resource in a manner approved by the Secretary.
